## Goal

Reproduce gh-76 (claim renewals push one ref per story, so a renewal tick costs N round trips), build a loop that goes red on it and confirm the cause. No fix.

## Progress

- **User side (live trace).** Main checkout's `.agents/norn/trace/2026-10-28.jsonl`, 1,621 ticks, avg tick ms by renewals in the tick: 0 → 3,740 (1,082 ticks), 1 → 11,173, 2 → 6,918, 5 → 14,524, 10 → 35,655 (70 ticks), 14 → 44,686. Cost grows with the number of renewals, as reported. (No real-gh dev-build run: claiming needs real issues; the loop below drives the same `runCli` tick path over a real bare git remote.)
- **Loop** (evidence `debug-gh76.test.ts`; copy to `packages/cli/test/` and run): `GH76_N=3 bun test packages/cli/test/debug-gh76.test.ts`. Harness with N issues, ticks until all N are claimed, advances the clock 4m, runs `norn tick --offline` with store's `setSpawnObserver` counting `git push` spawns that touch `refs/norn/claims/`. Asserts N renewals and exactly 1 claim push. Red: `renewals=3 ok=3 claim pushes=3` (one `push --porcelain --force-with-lease=refs/norn/claims/gh-K:<sha> origin <sha>:refs/norn/claims/gh-K` per story). ~15s, deterministic: N=1 green, N=2 red (2 pushes) on two runs, N=3 red (3), N=5 red (5). Minimised repro: 2 claimed stories, one renewal tick.
- **Confirmed cause.** The claim pushes are the only network calls in that tick (no fetch/ls-remote per renewal), and pushes == renewals for every N. Chain: `Actor.run` (`packages/cli/src/runtime/act/index.ts:72`) performs each decision alone → `claim` (`packages/cli/src/runtime/act/lifecycle.ts:156`) → `renewClaim` (`packages/store/src/refs.ts:176`) → `writeClaim` → `casRef` (`packages/store/src/git.ts:122`), one `git push` (line 129) + local `update-ref` per story.
- **Ruled out:** renewals spread over ticks (all N come due in one tick); extra remote reads per renewal (none observed).
- **Fix shape checked** (`git-batched-push-probe.txt`): one non-atomic `git push --porcelain --force-with-lease=A:x --force-with-lease=B:y origin s:A s:B` with B stale prints `+\t…:refs/norn/claims/gh-1\t… (forced update)` and `!\t…:refs/norn/claims/gh-2\t[rejected] (stale info)`, exits 1, and gh-1 is updated. So per-ref outcome must come from the porcelain lines, not the exit code.
- **Seams for regression tests.** Store: a batched CAS beside `casRef`/`renewClaim` tested in `packages/store/test/refs.test.ts` over real bare repos (all ok; one stale among several → only that one `stale`, others ok and mirrored locally; network failure → all `network`). Cli: the loop above as a tick-level test (N renewals → 1 claim push), and R1.2 in `recovery.test.ts` (one lost renewal still skips only that story's actions); its claim-lost transcript changes if spawns change. The actor must batch the side `claim` renew decisions before the per-decision loop (R1.2 order stays: renewals first, `lost` set per story).
- reproduce#1 reproduced: Reproduced: one renewal tick with N claimed stories makes N separate claim pushes (loop: N=2→2, 3→3, 5→5; asserts 1). Cause: Actor.run performs each claim decision alone → renewClaim → casRef, one git push per story. Live trace: avg tick 3.7s with 0 renewals, 35.7s with 10. Batched non-atomic push with per-ref porcelain verified to work.
